introduction: Vermont Crisis Fuel assists qualifying households facing a winter heating emergency. Contact intake before fuel is delivered or furnace work is completed.
description: Vermont Crisis Fuel assists qualifying households facing a winter heating emergency. Contact intake before fuel is delivered or furnace work is completed.

sections.who: The state lists income at or below 200% of federal poverty plus a heating crisis, such as being out of fuel without money to replace it.
sections.get: Help can cover the primary heating fuel, electricity needed for heating or arrangements to prevent loss of service.
sections.docs:
• Household income records.
  • Fuel account or heating-related electricity bill.
  • Details of the emergency and any shutoff notice.
sections.apply:
1. Call local intake first

    Contact the Community Action Agency through DCF Crisis Fuel for the document checklist.

  2. Confirm seasonal availability

    Bulk and metered fuels have different end dates; ask about the current season.

  3. Request emergency assessment

    Explain remaining fuel and deadlines before arranging a delivery or repair.
sections.after: Weekend and holiday assistance is limited to specified vulnerable households and seasonal dates. Check the current after-hours instructions.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DCF Crisis Fuel; After-hours instructions. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Can it reimburse fuel already delivered?
DCF says it cannot help after the fuel delivery or furnace work is completed.
A qualifying heating crisis is also required.
Call the agency first for intake instructions.
Is weekend intake open to everyone?
No. The state limits it to specified household groups and dates.
